          Man City vs PSG: Champions League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 12, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Wednesday's UEFA Champions League clash with our Man City vs PSG prediction and preview, as the two-time reigning European champions head to the Etihad Stadium.
Manchester City responded to a tumultuous couple of weeks on Sunday, as they beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield.

Man City fans in the away end soaked in the victory and revelled in their team's show of defiance, after the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League rules between 2009 and 2018. City have lodged an appeal, while awaiting news of a sanction.
Perhaps fittingly, then, it is another state-backed club next up for City, as they host Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Champions League.
PSG have gone from the Champions League's nearly men to two-time winners of the competition in the last couple of years.
Luis Enrique's team have not made the best of starts in Ligue 1, but they can probably afford a sluggish couple of months before clicking into gear.
They started their quest for a third straight Champions League crown in style with an emphatic 6-1 hammering of Slovan Bratislava last month.

Ousmane Dembélé became the third PSG player to score 2+ goals and provide 2+ assists in a Champions League game, after Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi; only Liverpool have also had three different players achieve this in the competition (Roberto Firmino, Mohamed Salah and Yossi Benayoun).

Dembélé has been directly involved in 31 goals in 41 Champions League games for PSG (20 goals, 11 assists), now the fifth most for the club in the competition, trailing only Mbappé (65 in 64 apps), Neymar (37 in 41 apps), Edinson Cavani (33 in 54 apps) and Ángel Di María (32 in 54 apps).

Former City forward Ferran Torres, meanwhile, became the first player to score a hat-trick on their Champions League debut for a side since Robert Lewandowski for Barcelona against Viktoria Plzen in September 2022.
PSG made the most high turnovers (14) and shot-ending high turnovers (7) of any side on MD1 of the new Champions League campaign, as well as averaging the most possession (72.1%).
But PSG's free-flowing attack will be tasked with breaking down a City defence that has already kept five clean sheets this term.
Not that City are lacking in the attacking department.

Rayan Cherki has averaged 4.1 defensive line-breaking passes per 90 for City in the Champions League. Since the start of last season, this is the second-highest average of any player in the competition (min. 300 minutes played), only behind Lee Kang-In (4.5).
And if he scores in this match, Erling Haaland will overtake Sergio Agüero (36 goals in 64 apps) to become City’s top scorer in the Champions League (Haaland currently on 36 goals in 40 apps).
Haaland has also scored 42 goals in 39 appearances in the group stage/league phase of the Champions League, the most of any player since his first season in the competition in 2019-20.
But the key to this contest could end up being who comes out on top in what promises to be an enthralling midfield tussle.
PSG's Vitinha has arguably been the top-performing midfielder in Europe over the past two seasons.
In fact, since the start of last season, Vitinha leads all midfielders in the Champions League for completed passes (1,703), line-breaking passes (327) and possession won (106 times).

But going up against PSG's mighty midfield will be City duo Enzo Fernández and Elliot Anderson. The latter, in particular, has had a fantastic start in a City shirt, as he looks to help fill the void left by Rodri's departure to Barcelona.
